headline: ASX MATERIALS POSTS SHARPEST LOSSES OF 2026 — Copper -1.3% to Four-Month Low $13,227/t; BHP -3.6%, Rio -2.5%, Southern Copper -4.1%, Freeport -4.7%
snippet: Tuesday's Australian session saw the ASX 200 Materials sector record its worst single-session performance of 2026 as copper, iron ore and lithium posted simultaneous breakdowns. LME copper slid 1.3% to $13,227.50/t — its lowest since July 8 — with iron ore falling roughly 4% and lithium ETFs tracking down 3–6% overnight. US-listed mining heavyweights fell sharply in sympathy: Southern Copper dropped 4.1% and Freeport-McMoRan fell 4.7%, while Australian dual-listed names BHP (-3.6%) and Rio Tinto (-2.5%) extended a multi-week drawdown. Analysts cited a triple-negative of AI investment concerns following the Nvidia CEO exit, a strengthening US dollar, and weaker-than-expected Chinese economic data as the primary drivers.

headline: PALADIN HOLDS FY2027 URANIUM GUIDANCE AT 5.1–5.6Mlb — Langer Heinrich Steady; Q1 Output Hit by Maintenance; PLS First Production 2031 Confirmed at AGM
snippet: Paladin Energy (TSX/ASX: PDN) held its 2026 annual general meeting on November 17 and confirmed FY2027 guidance unchanged: production 5.1–5.6 million pounds U3O8, sales 4.8–5.3Mlb, cost of production US$44–48 per pound, and capital expenditure US$29–35 million. Q1 FY2027 (July–September 2026) production came in at 1.00Mlb — below run-rate expectations due to a planned maintenance shutdown that pushed unit costs to US$61.60/lb for the period. FY2026 delivered 4.82Mlb at an average realised price of US$70.0/lb. Patterson Lake South (PLS), Paladin's next-generation Canadian asset acquired with Fission Uranium, has first production targeted for 2031 pending seasonal, regulatory and investment approvals.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,848 AFTER MONDAY'S MULTI-MONTH LOW — Slight Stabilization; Wednesday FOMC Minutes Are Next Binary Catalyst for Sector Recovery
snippet: Spot gold stabilized near US$3,848–$3,854 per ounce in Tuesday trading — a slight bounce from Monday's low of $3,832 but still the weakest level since October 2025. December gold futures settled 0.9% lower at $3,853 on Monday before the modest recovery. The technical picture remains fragile: bulls require a close above $4,010 to regain momentum, while a break below $3,800 would open the $3,700 support. Traders are now squarely focused on Wednesday's FOMC minutes as the next binary catalyst; any hawkish tone reaffirming Federal Reserve Chair Warsh's inflation-first stance would put renewed pressure on the sector, while dovish nuance could trigger the seasonally expected Q4 recovery.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER COMPLETES 54,579m/223-HOLE PHASE 2 AT MINTO, YUKON — Best Hole 9.3% Cu Over 5.4m; Feasibility Study Field Work Underway for 2027 Resource
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSX-V: SCMI) has completed its Phase 2 drill program at the former-producing Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Yukon, Canada — 54,579 metres in 223 holes totalling 109% of the planned 50,000 metres. High-grade results from the final holes include 9.3% Cu, 7.4 g/t Au and 54.9 g/t Ag over 5.4 metres at Minto North, and a broader interval of 44.7 metres grading 3.0% copper equivalent. Remaining assays are expected through fall and winter 2026, feeding an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate targeting Q1 2027. Feasibility study field work — including technical data collection for the planned restart — is now running in parallel with drilling completion, the first time Minto has advanced to this stage since Capstone Mining paused operations in 2023.

headline: ABEN GOLD YUKON: FIRST 2026 JUSTIN ASSAYS HIT 7.6m AT 3.66 g/t AU — Plus Tungsten By-Product; POW Discovery Zone Continuity Confirmed
snippet: Aben Gold Corp. (TSX-V: ABM) has released its first assay results from the 2026 drill program at the Justin gold-tungsten project in southeastern Yukon, with the standout interval returning 7.6 metres grading 3.66 g/t gold, together with anomalous tungsten by-product values, confirming down-dip continuity of the POW Discovery Zone first defined in 2025. The 2026 program — approximately 1,300 metres in targeted diamond holes funded from Aben's existing treasury — also returns the project to investor attention at a time when junior gold drill plays are seeing selective re-rating even amid the broader sector selloff. The Justin project sits in the same prolific Selwyn Basin mineral trend as several active Yukon exploration plays.

headline: EX-CHINA RARE EARTH SUPPLY CHAIN ADVANCES — Malaysia Issues First REE Export Permit; Neo Performance Materials' Estonia NdFeB Magnet Plant Goes Live
snippet: SMM's rare earth weekly review for the week of November 17 flags two significant ex-China supply chain milestones: Malaysia has issued its first rare earth product export permit, opening a new trade channel outside of Chinese licensing, while Neo Performance Materials has started commercial production at its NdFeB permanent magnet plant in Sillamäe, Estonia — the first Western-European-scale magnet facility capable of processing rare earths without routing through Chinese downstream processors. Light rare earth (Pr-Nd) FOB and CIF quotes were broadly raised in the week, with spot prices reacting to the tighter ex-China licensing regime.

headline: URANIUM DEMAND EFFECTIVELY DOUBLING — But New Mine Development Takes 10-20 Years; Structural Supply Gap Widens as Nuclear Builds Outpace Exploration Capex
snippet: Crux Investor's latest uranium market analysis frames the supply-demand imbalance in structural rather than cyclical terms: global uranium demand is effectively doubling when you account for reactor restarts, life extensions, and the new wave of nuclear builds tied to AI data centre power commitments, while the lead time for a greenfield uranium mine from discovery to first production averages 10–20 years. The analysis argues that the current uranium price near US$91.85/lb is not fully discounting the gap between announced nuclear capacity additions and the exploration capex needed to bring sufficient new mines online in time, and identifies Athabasca Basin, Namibia and Kazakhstan-adjacent projects as the most likely sources of swing supply.

headline: CHINA ZERO-EXPORTS RARE EARTHS TO JAPAN FOR THIRD STRAIGHT MONTH — European Spot Dysprosium at $3,200-4,200/kg vs. $215-220/kg Domestic China
snippet: Crux Investor documents the third consecutive month of near-zero Chinese rare earth exports to Japan across controlled heavy rare earth elements including dysprosium, terbium and yttrium — a supply squeeze that has lasted longer than most Western analysts expected when China's April 2025 export controls were introduced. The price divergence is stark: European spot dysprosium oxide is now quoted at US$3,200–4,200 per kilogram while Chinese domestic prices remain near US$215–220/kg, a 15–20x gap that reflects the difficulty of routing ex-China supply through alternative processing chains. For TSX-V and ASX rare earth explorers outside China, the spread represents the strongest economic argument for accelerating development since the 2011 REE boom.

headline: DAURA GOLD EARNS INTO ARGENTINA'S DESEADO MASSIF — Binding LOI With Latin Metals for Cerro Bayo/La Flora; Up to 80% via Staged Spending
snippet: Daura Gold Corp. (TSX-V: DGC) has entered a binding letter agreement with Latin Metals Inc. to earn up to an 80% interest in the Cerro Bayo and La Flora projects located in Patagonia's Deseado Massif, Argentina — a district with a proven track record of high-grade epithermal gold-silver deposits (Coeur's Joaquin mine, Patagonia Gold's Cap-Oeste, and Silver Spruce's nearby targets). The earn-in structure involves staged spending commitments over multiple years; full terms and the work program were not disclosed in the initial announcement. The Deseado Massif is recognised as one of South America's premier exploration corridors for high-grade bulk-tonnage and bonanza-grade epithermal gold-silver systems.
